questions.question:
In the following question, select the number which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.

 
 

 
 
6

 
 
 
5

 
 
 
22

 
 
 

 
 
2

 
 
 
3

 
 
 
10

 
 
 

 
 
6

 
 
 
2

 
 
 
?
questions.solution:
The followed pattern is,

Add the 1st and 2ⁿd column and multiply the resultant by 2 to get the 3rd column.

In row 1,

6 + 5 = 11, 11 × 2 = 22

In row 2,

2 + 3 = 5, 5 × 2 = 10

Thus, in row 3,

6 + 2 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16

Hence, 16 is the correct alternative.

questions.question: If 12 % 6 ÷ 3 = 15 and 15 % 3 ÷ 4 = 14, then 17 % 6 ÷ 2 = ?
questions.solution:
The followed pattern is,

% stands for + and ÷ stands for -.

12 % 6 ÷ 3 = 15 → 12 + 6 - 3 = 18 - 3 = 15

15 % 3 ÷ 4 = 14 → 15 + 3 - 4 = 18 - 4 = 14

Thus,

17 % 6 ÷ 2 = ? → 17 + 6 - 2 = 23 - 2 = 21

Hence, 21 is the correct alternative.

questions.question: Present age of A is 48 years. 7 years hence, ages of A and B will be in ratio 5 : 6. What is the present age (in years) of B?
questions.solution:
The present age of A = 48 years

Age of A after 7 years = 55

The ratio of the age of A and B after 7 years = 5 : 6

According to the question,

(5)/(6) = frac{{55}}{x}

⇒ x = 66

Hence, present age of B = (66 - 7) years = 59 years

questions.question: Weight of P is thrice that of Q. Weight of Q is ½ of R. Weight of R is 4 times of S. Weight of S is 1/5 of T. Who is the lightest?
questions.solution:
According to the given data, their order in descending order is,

Weight of P is thrice that of Q.

P = 3 Q → P > Q

Weight of Q is ½ of R.

Q = 1/2 R → R > Q

Weight of R is 4 times of S.

R = 4 S → R > S

Weight of S is 1/5 of T.

S = 1/5 T → T > S

Here if we consider S as 1,

S = 1, then T = 5, R = 4, Q = 2 and P = 6

Thus,

P > T > R > Q > S

Hence, ‘S’ is the lightest one among all.

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All cups are plates.

II. All books are cups.

**Conclusions:**

I. All plates are books.

II. All books are plates.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bf40f2e207f70c80ecfa5105da10c4d618d3bc04125896e3fab6445a92e6bee.png] **

**Conclusions:**

I. All plates are books → False (It is possible but not definite.)

II. All books are plates → True (as shown in the above figure)

Hence, only conclusion II follows.
